# Commands

`edna2dwc <command> --help` gives each command's options. This page lists the commands, as `edna2dwc --help` groups them, and shows how they fit together.

## Every command

<!-- generated by `just docs` from the command docstrings in edna2dwc/cli/: edit the code, not this table -->
```text
What you do:
  inspect           Look at your data files and write INSPECTION.md listing the terms an archive
                    could fill.
  resolve-taxonomy  Resolve each lineage in occurrence_long.tsv against the registers, under the
                    taxonomy settings in answers.yaml.
  build             Build the archive from answers.yaml, conversion.yaml, occurrence_long.tsv,
                    resolved_taxonomy.tsv, confirmed/, audit_record.json, assembly.json and the
                    files answers.yaml names.
  evaluate          Check a finished archive and write EVALUATION.md saying what it lacks.

Set up:
  doctor       Check that this install is complete, and say where it is.
  credentials  Store the GBIF account 'evaluate --gbif' and 'validate --gbif' sign in with.
  init         Start a conversion: write answers.yaml, conversion.yaml and the justfile in this
               directory.

Read inputs into one table:
  text                   Print the text of a PDF, DOCX, XLSX or text file, so nobody writes a parser
                         to read one.
  detect-redundant       Fingerprint each input and report which pairs look like duplicates.
  record-step            Add a reader script to the steps: log in conversion.yaml, so replay runs it
                         before build.
  assemble               Join the tables a reader script wrote into occurrence_long.tsv, and record
                         the step.
  validate-intermediate  Check that an occurrence_long.tsv file satisfies the intermediate table's
                         schema.

Review and reproduce a conversion:
  validate  Check an archive's structure, term names, value formats, and the terms that must appear
            together.
  audit     Check that every value in the archive came from somewhere.
  findings  Explain finding codes: every code, or only the ones given.
  replay    Reproduce a conversion from conversion.yaml, or compare two archives.

Assemble an archive from tables already in Darwin Core terms:
  package  Assemble a Darwin Core Archive from tables that already use Darwin Core terms.

Maintenance:
  terms  Maintain the vendored term table by hand. Never run in CI.
```

`doctor` checks more than `--version` can. It prints where the install lives, so with two installs you can tell which one answered, and it checks that the packages a reader script may import and the tool's own modules load. An incomplete or stale install can still report a plausible version number.

It also prints the memory limit and where it came from, and the free space in the directory DuckDB spills to. `doctor --json` gives them as `memory_limit`, `memory_limit_source`, `spill_dir` and `spill_free_bytes`. See [Memory and disk](#memory-and-disk).

## The five stages

A conversion goes through five stages, and each conversion command ends its output with the stage it is at, such as `Stage 3 of 5: Read`, and a `Next:` line naming the next step. `init` and the `build` before an audit name the stage the next step starts, because the tool reports Read only once a reader script is recorded, and Check only once an audit is. `INSPECTION.md` lists the stages, and `REVIEW.md` ticks them off.

| | Stage | What happens | Commands |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Inspect | Find what data the files contain, and which fields GBIF and OBIS need that they lack | `doctor`, `inspect` |
| 2 | Describe | Give the dataset's title, people and license, and what each marker targets | `init`, then `answers.yaml` |
| 3 | Read | Read the files into one table, one row per sequence per sample | `record-step`, `assemble` |
| 4 | Convert | Match the names to WoRMS and GBIF, build the archive and review its proposals | `resolve-taxonomy`, `build` |
| 5 | Check | Audit and validate the archive, and go over the fields it is still missing | `audit record`, `evaluate` |

`build` is at Convert until an audit is recorded, then at Check, so the stage never moves backwards. What still blocks the archive is listed under "Waiting on you" in `REVIEW.md`.

## A conversion

A conversion directory holds the files a person owns and the files the tool writes. Nothing the tool writes is a file a person edits.

| File | Written by | What it holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `answers.yaml` | `init`, once, then the person | The dataset metadata, what each marker amplifies, which ambiguous samples are controls, and every setting |
| `occurrence_long.tsv` | `assemble`, from the tables a reader script wrote | The intermediate table |
| `resolved_taxonomy.tsv` | `resolve-taxonomy` | The taxonomy resolved from the registers. `build` reads it and doesn't call a register |
| `proposed/` | every `build`, from scratch | What the tool proposes, for a person to review |
| `confirmed/` | the person | The rows of a proposal a person changed, applied over the proposal |
| `conversion.yaml` | `init`, `record-step`, `assemble`, `resolve-taxonomy`, `build` | The reader scripts, the raw inputs, the recorded environment, and when and against which registers the taxonomy was resolved |
| `REVIEW.md` | every `build` | What is waiting on a person, and how to close it |

Run `resolve-taxonomy` once the intermediate table is written, and again after the table or the `taxonomy` settings in `answers.yaml` change. `resolve-taxonomy -o trial.tsv` writes a trial file instead, to compare a setting without replacing `resolved_taxonomy.tsv`.

`build` stops before writing the archive if `answers.yaml` lacks the dataset `metadata`, a marker's target under `markers`, an answer under `controls` for a sample whose ID only weakly matches a control keyword, `filters.exclude_human` when the table has human reads, or `organismQuantityType` when a count isn't a whole number. It asks for every missing answer at once, and `REVIEW.md` names each key to set.

`build` exits 1 when it ends in `error`, 2 when it refuses `answers.yaml`, the intermediate table or a confirmed sheet, and 0 otherwise. An error starts with `Error:`. `REVIEW.md` is written every time.

## What `build` does

`build` recomputes the archive every time. It runs these steps in this order:

| Step | Proposal it writes | Confirmed sheet it applies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Classify samples as controls | `proposed/control_roster.tsv` | none: `controls:` in `answers.yaml` settles a sample |
| Propose the term mapping | `proposed/term_mapping.tsv` | `confirmed/term_mapping.tsv` |
| Derive lineages, and stop if `resolved_taxonomy.tsv` is absent or lacks one | | |
| Join the taxonomy | `proposed/taxa.tsv` | `confirmed/taxa.tsv` |
| Remove controls and excluded taxa | | |
| Apply the mapping and constants | | |
| Derive status, quantities, coordinates and country | `proposed/derived_values.tsv` | `confirmed/derived_values.tsv` |
| Build `occurrenceID` | | |
| Record each term's state | | |
| Write the archive, validate it, write the report and bundle `reproduce/` | | |

[Controls and exclusions](controls-and-exclusions.md), [Term mapping](term-mapping.md), [Taxonomy](taxonomy.md) and [Derived fields](derived-fields.md) cover the steps.

## Reviewing a proposal

`REVIEW.md` lists a proposal as waiting when it has something to review:

| Proposal | Waits for review when |
| --- | --- |
| `control_roster.tsv` | a sample is excluded on a keyword in its ID alone, and `controls:` doesn't answer it |
| `term_mapping.tsv` | a mapping is ambiguous, or a column goes to `dynamicProperties` or eMoF |
| `taxa.tsv` | always |
| `derived_values.tsv` | a coordinate sign looks wrong |

To review the roster, answer its samples under `controls:`. To review another proposal, write a sheet of the same name in `confirmed/` with the proposal's header and only the rows you change, and run `build` again. A header alone accepts the proposal:

```bash
mkdir -p confirmed
head -1 proposed/taxa.tsv > confirmed/taxa.tsv
edna2dwc build
```

A confirmed sheet is applied over the fresh proposal by key: the source column of a mapping row, the `lineage_key` of a taxon, and the `sampleID` and `featureID` of a derived row. Its rows win, and rows it leaves out follow the proposal on every build, so a later fix to the input reaches them. A row whose key the table no longer has is reported as `CONFIRMED_ROW_UNMATCHED`, or `DERIVED_CONFIRMED_UNMATCHED` in `derived_values.tsv`, and the report lists every sheet applied as `CONFIRMED_SHEET_APPLIED`.

Each row of `confirmed/term_mapping.tsv`, `confirmed/taxa.tsv` or `confirmed/derived_values.tsv` that changes the proposal fills two columns, which are empty in the proposal. `provenance` says what the change rests on, such as `methods.pdf p3, the genus was misidentified`. A changed row with nothing in `provenance` refuses the sheet, and the build names the row. `confirmed` is a person's reply, pasted as they gave it, such as `J. Smith: yes`. A changed row with `confirmed` empty is applied, and holds the build at `needs_review` until a person confirms it. `REVIEW.md` reports each applied sheet as `N row(s) changed, M not confirmed`.

`build --automatic` uses every proposal nobody confirmed as written, and logs each as `PROPOSAL_ACCEPTED`. It also uses every answer and confirmed row with `confirmed` empty, and logs one `UNCONFIRMED_ACCEPTED` naming them. It never fills in a missing answer, accepts a blank required metadata field or accepts a validator issue. Use it when there is nobody to ask.

## Logging every command

Set `EDNA2DWC_LOG` to a file path and every command appends one JSON line to it: the arguments, when it started, how many seconds it took, its exit code, the codes of the findings it raised, any error message, and the requests it made to WoRMS and GBIF, with each failed request counted by its HTTP status or error type, such as `"worms failed: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests": 3`. A relative path is taken from where the first command ran, so the steps `replay` runs log to the same file. A missing directory is created; if the file still can't be written, the command prints one warning and keeps its exit code. Nothing is logged when the variable is unset.

## Memory and disk

Each command works in a DuckDB database under a memory limit, and writes what doesn't fit to the system temporary directory. The limit is half the memory the process can use: the machine's memory, or a container's limit when that is lower. Peak memory follows the limit, not the number of rows; on Linux the process peaks up to about 600 MB above it.

Set `EDNA2DWC_MEMORY_LIMIT` to change the limit, such as `EDNA2DWC_MEMORY_LIMIT=2GB`. Set `TMPDIR` to spill to a larger disk. A command that runs out of either stops with one line naming the limit, the free space and both settings. See [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md#a-command-runs-out-of-memory-or-disk).
